scenario: Adopt Lintwise as a required pre-merge check (eight engineers)

motion.text: The team adopts Lintwise, an automated code-quality checker, as a required pre-merge check on every repository.

research: Priya: pull Lintwise's default rule manifest on our actual monorepo to confirm whether secret-pattern and vulnerable-dependency rules are enabled by default, run at error severity, and fire without extra configuration.

Elena: verify in a dry run against a known-bad test commit (hard-coded key) that Lintwise's secret-detection rule set catches it by default, and confirm those findings cannot be downgraded to warning via config or opt-out.

Sana: run a two-week advisory (non-blocking) pass of Lintwise scoped to two-to-three representative pipeline directories; record per-check false-positive count, true-positive count, wall-clock delta against the 11-minute CI baseline, and readability of finding messages for a junior developer.

Olga: confirm whether Lintwise finding messages are self-explanatory enough to act on in under a minute without consulting external docs; check with Sana whether her pilot data captures message clarity alongside FP counts.

chairQuestions.topic: Lintwise wall-clock runtime and parallel-vs-serial execution on a multi-developer monorepo
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Priya ran Lintwise for six months on a team repo. She cited a 4-minute CI hit; Tom cited 2 minutes. I need the actual median wall-clock time per PR and whether Lintwise ran concurrently with the existing build or after it finished.

chairQuestions.topic: Default ruleset contents: security/secret detection vs style-only rules, and observed false-positive rate
chairQuestions.experience_sought: Tom ran Lintwise on his side project. I need to know whether the default enabled rules included secret-pattern and vulnerable-dependency checks, or only style/null-safety nits, and roughly what fraction of its warnings were actionable fixes versus noise he had to dismiss.
